tour.title: Project Overview & Domain
tour.description: Start with the README to learn what enphase-monitor is: a Go CLI that pulls solar energy data from the Enlighten Cloud API v4, enriches it with weather, and reports true-up totals. CONTEXT.md complements it with the domain glossary you will see throughout the code — Site, System, Query Mode, Net Flow, and the API Budget that governs how often the tool may call the cloud. Read these first so the package names later make immediate sense.

tour.title: Getting Started
tour.description: QUICKSTART.md walks a new user from clone to first run, and the Makefile defines the build/run/test/setup targets that wrap the Go toolchain. Together they show the project's outer interface before you open any source file. Note the setup target, which launches the interactive OAuth wizard you will meet again in the orchestration layer.
tour.languageLesson: Makefile targets define build steps with dependency tracking. Phony targets (build, test, setup) name actions rather than files, so they always run when invoked.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: main.go is the process entry point and the spine of the whole tour: it parses flags, loads config and credentials, initializes location/weather, then dispatches to one of several workflows (runner, backfill, true-up, setup, cache-report, refresh-token). This is the single file with the broadest reach — every execution mode begins here. Read it as a table of contents for the rest of the codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Go programs start at func main() in package main. An init guard pattern checks for required config/credentials early and exits with a clear message before any work begins.

tour.title: Flags & Configuration
tour.description: Building on the dispatch in main.go, this step covers how user intent and settings are captured. flags.go defines the command-line surface and query-mode selection, while config.go and credentials.go load the YAML files — config.yaml for systems and display colors, and the gitignored credentials.yaml for API keys and OAuth tokens. The example templates show the exact shape a user must fill in.

tour.title: Shared Constants & Types
tour.description: constants.go has the highest fan-in in the entire project (depended on by 43 nodes): it centralizes query modes, API endpoints, and the rate-limit/budget values that the whole codebase reads. types.go defines SystemConfig and APIConfig, the cross-package structs that break import cycles between config and the API layer. Understanding this shared vocabulary now makes every later package easier to read.

tour.title: Execution Modes & Orchestration
tour.description: runner.go drives the once and continuous monitoring modes, and setup.go is the interactive OAuth onboarding wizard reached from the Makefile setup target. These orchestrators do little computation themselves — they wire together the domain, integration, and infrastructure packages that the remaining steps explore. This is where main.go's dispatch decisions turn into real work.

tour.title: Multi-System Aggregation
tour.description: aggregator.go is the core combine step: it fetches metrics for every configured Enphase system through the cloud clients, handling credential-pool failover, rate limiting, and context cancellation. types.go in the same package defines AggregatedMetrics, DailyWeather, and TrueUpReport — the result structures (16 fan-in each) that carry combined energy and weather data through the rest of the app. This is the heart of the domain layer.

tour.title: Cloud API, Cache & Budget
tour.description: client.go is the Enlighten Cloud API v4 client, fetching per-date energy, production, consumption, and battery metrics via interval and lifetime endpoints. Crucially, every call routes through cache.go, which persists responses to disk and enforces the rolling API Budget so the tool stays under Enphase's 10-requests-per-minute limit. urlbuilder.go constructs the cache-stable request URLs that make this layered caching reliable.

tour.title: OAuth & Credential Pool
tour.description: Authenticated calls need tokens. oauth.go and authorization.go manage the OAuth 2.0 flow and token refresh, while pool.go maintains a rotatable pool of credential sets, selecting one per system and failing over to the next when a key hits a 429 rate-limit response. This round-robin pooling is what lets the tool spread its monthly request budget across multiple Enphase keys.

tour.title: True-Up Reporting
tour.description: trueup.go computes the annual true-up report — the net energy balance over the utility billing year that determines what a solar customer owes or is credited. It consumes the AggregatedMetrics and TrueUpReport types from Step 7 and relies on timezone.go to compute the correct true-up period boundaries. This is one of the project's headline outputs.

tour.title: Historical Backfill & Weather Enrichment
tour.description: This cluster is the project's analysis end-goal: a year of per-day energy-plus-weather records for correlation. backfill.go orchestrates the historical sweep, history.go shapes the per-day records, and weather.go plus geocode.go and location.go resolve a site's coordinates and pull matching Open-Meteo daily weather. Together they turn raw cloud telemetry into an exportable, structured dataset.

tour.title: Output & Validation Mode
tour.description: Finally, display.go formats the aggregated results into colorized terminal tables (using the color settings loaded back in Step 4), and validation.go implements Validation Mode, which re-fetches data bypassing the cache to confirm cached values match the live API. The .golangci.yml linter config rounds out the picture, showing the static-analysis standards every file in this tour is held to.
